correctness.rationale: The Boolean threshold proof is quantified for arbitrary index sets: any weakly compact approximation within 1/2 would make the Boolean columns a continuous pointwise transform of a relatively weakly compact set in C(beta J), therefore relatively weakly compact by dominated convergence and Eberlein--Smulian. The Krein convex-hull theorem then makes the operator weakly compact. The 1/2 rank-one upper bound is exact. For injective f the left-quotient support formulas are exhaustive, disjointness proves a Hilbert-space factorization with bounds 1 and square-root 2, and 1-separated derivatives prove noncompactness. The half-graph has noncommuting iterated limits, proving failure of weak compactness. The approximation tail is explicitly cited as prior.
